title: A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical

concept.text: The innovation would be a controlled laboratory experiment that establishes nonclassical features of gravitational dynamics under explicit, experimentally justified assumptions. Its central task is to measure correlations between two masses and show that their gravitational interaction produces results consistent with specified quantum predictions and inconsistent with concrete classical-gravity alternatives.

In the original spatial-superposition approach, each mass occupies a quantum superposition of different positions. Different combinations of positions experience different gravitational interactions, accumulating different quantum phases. These phases can entangle the masses: their joint quantum state then cannot be described as independent states of the two objects. Bose and collaborators proposed using spin measurements to witness the resulting entanglement in adjacent matter-wave interferometers.

The inference from entanglement to nonclassical gravity requires care. The 2017 proposal presents entanglement as evidence for a quantum mediator, while Di Biagio's 2025–2026 analysis argues that additional assumptions enter this conclusion and that detecting gravity-induced entanglement alone does not exclude every classical-field description. The experimental target is therefore quantitative comparison of concrete theories. An alternative correlation observable could serve the same goal only with a specific argument showing what its measurement excludes.

significance.text: A convincing result would give experimental access to the character of the gravitational interaction between quantum systems. Agreement with low-energy quantum-gravity predictions, together with exclusion of specified classical alternatives, would supply a direct empirical constraint on how gravity and quantum matter fit together. The immediate advance would be a measured distinction between competing descriptions of gravitational dynamics, with the strength of the conclusion determined by the assumptions and alternatives tested.

Interpretive synthesis: the photoelectric effect offers a useful analogy for the potential impact. A laboratory result could make quantum features necessary in an account of gravity before a complete theory exists. The analogy has limits: excluding selected classical models would not establish that every conceivable classical description fails, and a single correlation measurement would not automatically settle the interpretation of the gravitational field.

The proposed experiment probes a low-energy regime in which gravitationally induced phases and correlations can be calculated. A successful measurement could guide further theory and more discriminating experiments, but it would not by itself determine a complete ultraviolet theory or establish the behavior of gravity at the Planck scale.

Scope synthesis: consequences for black-hole information would require additional theoretical and observational work connecting the laboratory result to black-hole evaporation. Controlled wormholes and new energy sources do not follow from demonstrating nonclassical gravitational dynamics. These are limits on the inference and prospective impact, rather than reasons to discount the foundational importance of a successful experiment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing experimental capability is a sufficiently controlled interaction between quantum masses to resolve gravitationally generated correlations while preserving the coherence needed to produce them. In the original proposal, both spatial and spin degrees of freedom must remain coherent throughout the experiment. The masses, separations, superposition sizes, and interaction duration must jointly produce a detectable gravitational phase without making competing interactions or environmental disturbances dominant.

The engineering barrier includes quantifying and suppressing electromagnetic and Casimir–Polder interactions, as well as decoherence from gas collisions and other environmental effects. These contributions must be bounded tightly enough that they cannot explain an apparent signal or erase the sought correlation. In Bose's illustrative estimates, the Casimir–Polder contribution is approximately one tenth of gravity, and the collisional decoherence time is comparable to the experiment's duration. Those estimates illustrate a demanding control problem; they do not establish that all backgrounds are already negligible.

A second barrier is interpretive and computational: competing quantum and classical descriptions must yield detailed predictions for the actual apparatus. Di Biagio's analysis motivates comparing dependence on mass, separation, interaction duration, entanglement, and decoherence, rather than treating the presence of entanglement as a universal dividing line. The analysis must identify which assumptions support the inference and which classical alternatives remain distinguishable within experimental uncertainty.

current_state.text: The Bose–Marletto–Vedral class of proposals dates to 2017. The supplied Bose paper, published as Physical Review Letters 119, 240401, calculates that two micron-scale test masses in adjacent matter-wave interferometers could become detectably entangled through gravitational phase evolution. It also acknowledges Marletto and Vedral's independent work. This is a theoretical mechanism and experimental proposal, rather than a report of realized gravitational entanglement.

Di Biagio's analysis was initially posted in 2025 and revised on 16 September 2026. The supplied review reports that the arXiv landing page describes the revised work as accepted for publication in Physical Review D. That metadata supports reported acceptance, without independently establishing the publication date. The paper argues that bare detection of gravity-induced entanglement is insufficient for a theory-independent conclusion and advocates quantitative tests of concrete gravitational theories. This is an attributed theoretical analysis; the supplied material does not establish consensus that every classical-field calculation discussed is correct.

The supplied evidence does not establish the complete experimental situation as of 1 November 2026. In particular, it does not substantiate the earlier assertions that no gravity-induced entanglement had been reported by that date, that the original apparatus requirements remained unmet then, or that levitated-nanoparticle work had established a relevant millisecond-scale coherence capability. The dated proposals and prospective discussion cannot establish an exhaustive absence of subsequent experimental results. These gaps leave those assertions unresolved rather than demonstrating that they are false.

The supplied review reports complete, untruncated full-paper extractions for both theoretical papers, with no extraction issues recorded in the source index. The arXiv landing-page evidence used for acceptance metadata contains an abstract and bibliographic information rather than the full paper. The principal limitation on the current-state assessment is the absence of an experimental survey or bounded freshness search in the supplied evidence, rather than an identified extraction failure in the reviewed papers.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: measure gravitationally generated correlations that agree quantitatively with specified low-energy quantum-gravity predictions and exclude named classical-gravity alternatives at stated statistical confidence over stated parameter ranges. Predictions should describe the experimental setup closely enough to compare both the sought correlations and relevant decoherence. Di Biagio's discussion motivates this model-comparison approach, but does not provide an exhaustive catalogue of all possible classical theories.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting requirements: publish the masses, separations, spatial-superposition sizes, interaction durations, coherence times, measurement procedures, uncertainties, and bounds on non-gravitational interactions and environmental decoherence. The analysis should show why residual backgrounds cannot account for the measured correlations and should make the assumptions behind any inference about the mediator explicit. If an observable other than entanglement is used, its discriminatory power must be justified for the models under test.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reporting requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility criterion: obtain two independently replicated experimental demonstrations with compatible conclusions and sufficiently documented methods and data for external scrutiny. This is a proposed reliability threshold for this record, not an established standard prescribed by the supplied papers. Measurements across multiple settings would establish the demonstrated breadth of the result; finite tests would not prove that every possible classical-field theory is impossible.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility criterion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: a stronger constraint on collapse models, improved coherence of massive objects, or atomic interferometry in Earth's gravity would be valuable enabling or adjacent results, but would not alone supply the required discrimination of the interaction between quantum masses. A Page-curve calculation would likewise address a different theoretical question. Such results could contribute to the program without satisfying this proposed completion criterion by themselves.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PHY-11, “A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox,” is the closest conceptual neighbor because both concern the relationship between gravity and quantum physics. PHY-03 concerns laboratory discrimination of gravitational dynamics; PHY-11's title points to a tested account of information in black-hole processes. A successful tabletop result could constrain relevant theory, but would not alone establish a resolution of black-hole evaporation. Only PHY-11's title is supplied, so a more detailed division of scope remains unverified.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-05, “A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale,” also concerns fundamental gravitational physics, while PHY-04, “Laboratory identification of the dark-matter particle,” concerns the identity of matter inferred from gravitational phenomena. Establishing nonclassical gravitational dynamics would not by itself explain the dark-energy scale or identify a dark-matter particle. The three entries ask distinct questions even if future theories connect their answers.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-06, discovery of a magnetic monopole; PHY-07, observation of baryon-number violation; PHY-08, observation of lepton-number violation; PHY-12, identification of the physics setting the Higgs-mass scale; and PHY-13, a tested mechanism for the cosmic matter excess, share the broader aim of experimentally distinguishing fundamental theories. Their defining observations concern particles, symmetries, mass scales, or cosmological mechanisms. None is interchangeable with a controlled test of gravitationally generated correlations between quantum masses.

Roster-based synthesis: PHY-01, room-temperature superconducting conductors at ambient pressure; PHY-02, sustained net-electric fusion power; PHY-09, a coherent gamma-ray source; and PHY-10, collider-quality plasma wakefield acceleration, define material, energy, radiation-source, or accelerator capabilities. They may belong to the same broad landscape of experimental physics, but their completion criteria are independent of PHY-03. Demonstrating nonclassical gravity would not establish any of those practical capabilities.

change_log.change: Preserved PHY-03's identity and title while defining the outcome through explicit assumptions and quantitative comparison of quantum and classical gravitational predictions.
change_log.reason: The review supports the laboratory objective but finds that entanglement detection alone does not establish a theory-independent exclusion of every classical description.

change_log.change: Explained spatial superpositions, gravitational phase accumulation, entanglement, and the proposed spin witness.
change_log.reason: These details make the physical mechanism understandable without requiring the reader to consult the research or review.

change_log.change: Replaced an unspecified equivalent nonclassical correlation with a requirement for a justified alternative observable.
change_log.reason: A correlation is useful only if its relationship to the competing theories and inference assumptions is established.

change_log.change: Recast negligible backgrounds as a control objective and incorporated the approximate one-tenth Casimir–Polder contribution and comparable collisional decoherence timescale.
change_log.reason: The reviewed estimates illustrate unresolved experimental demands rather than demonstrated elimination of competing effects.

change_log.change: Qualified the claimed absence of experimental reports, unmet apparatus requirements, and millisecond-scale nanoparticle coherence.
change_log.reason: The supplied papers and empty freshness record do not establish those claims through 1 November 2026; this limitation does not show that the claims are false.

change_log.change: Distinguished Di Biagio's dated theoretical argument and reported Physical Review D acceptance from a verified publication date or established consensus.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports the attributed argument and acceptance metadata, with narrower implications than a settled experimental or theoretical verdict.

change_log.change: Removed the universal assertion about every laboratory test to date and qualified the photoelectric-effect analogy.
change_log.reason: The sources do not establish the universal historical claim, and the analogy must preserve the difference between bounded model exclusion and an assumption-free conclusion.

change_log.change: Made completion criteria assessable through named alternatives, parameter ranges, uncertainty, controls, and independent replication.
change_log.reason: These are proposed criteria grounded in the experimental goal, not source-prescribed standards or guarantees of universal exclusion.

change_log.change: Integrated all roster entries through explicit overlaps and distinctions, including the supplied PHY-11 title.
change_log.reason: The roster permits a broad comparison with PHY-11, while its title alone cannot verify a detailed allocation of scope.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether gravity-induced entanglement had been experimentally reported by 1 November 2026 or the apparatus capabilities available on that date.
The claimed millisecond-scale coherence assessment for levitated nanoparticles lacks supporting evidence in the supplied materials.
A concrete experimental design still needs a named set of classical alternatives, their predictions, parameter ranges, uncertainty thresholds, and explicit inference assumptions.
The supplied review does not establish consensus on the correctness or scope of the classical-field calculations discussed by Di Biagio.
The exact Physical Review D publication date is not independently established by the reported acceptance metadata.
Only roster titles are supplied for related innovations; detailed scope boundaries, especially with PHY-11, remain unverified.
